text:
Olivia - CS: heads up — ParcelGo reported their ingest service throwing JSON parse errors after the 02:00 rollout. They say the body now starts with a short preface string and their strict validator bails.
Olivia - CS: sample snippet from the response body they pasted: 
```
PREFIX_1234:{"order_id": "abc123", "items": [...] }
```
Olivia - CS: they see this in ~15% of requests since the canary flip. Impact: automatic downstream unmarshal fails, entire batch rejected.
Ben - Infra: can you paste the request id / example full response headers and whether this was Hosted or Dedicated?
Olivia - CS: request ids: r-20240315-8f3a, r-20240315-8f8b (both attached). Customer is on Hosted API.
deploy-bot: deploy v3.14.2 -> prod started 2024-03-15T01:45Z; canary -> 10% -> 02:00Z -> 50% at 02:30Z.
Meera - ML: hmm, that prefix looks like the new telemetry envelope we shipped for model traces. There's a change in the response formatter that prepends `PREFIX_<trace_id>:` when envelope mode is enabled. Shouldn't be on by default for production API customers.
Ben - Infra: ok. Does anyone know which config toggle controls that? Could be a new feature flag flipped during rollout.
Meera - ML: it's `response_envelope: trace_id_prefix` in the response adapter. I see a recent PR that added it with default off, but the deployment job's config merge accidentally injected `response_envelope: auto` into the Hosted runtime patch.
Ben - Infra: thanks. Immediate mitigation: we can push a proxy filter to strip leading `^PREFIX_[A-Za-z0-9]+:` before handing to customers' apps. Quick regex fix will be less risky than a full rollback.
Ben - Infra: patch ready: infra/patches/strip-prefix-2024-03-15, will deploy to edge proxies in ~10m.
Olivia - CS: ParcelGo is requesting a hotfix or rollback — they want ETA and whether we can reprocess the failed batches.
Meera - ML: rolling back the config change from the canary is also required. I'll open a rollback PR for the response adapter to revert the `response_envelope` merge.
Ben - Infra: deploying proxy patch now (rolling, low risk). If that clears their errors we can avoid full rollback.
Ben - Infra: command I'm running: `kubectl -n edge rollout restart deployment/edge-proxy && kubectl logs -f deploy/edge-proxy | grep strip-prefix`
Olivia - CS: I'll message ParcelGo, tell them we have a patch going to edge in ~10m and can reprocess once cleared. They asked if tokens/timestamps leaked in the prefix — they said prefix is opaque id only.
Meera - ML: confirmed prefix contains only trace id, no model output. No sensitive data.
Olivia - CS: ParcelGo also wants us to backfill 48 failed batches, can we coordinate?
Ben - Infra: once proxy patch shows no more prefixed responses in staging, we can coordinate a backfill window. I will monitor error rate.
deploy-bot: rollout patch/strip-prefix to edge-proxy succeeded at 2024-03-15T02:12Z.
Ben - Infra: edge patch deployed. Monitoring… error rate for ParcelGo ingestion down from 14% -> 0.6% in last 5m.
Olivia - CS: ParcelGo confirms ingest succeeded for new requests, asking for an SLA credit and confirmation about a permanent fix.
Meera - ML: PR opened to revert accidental config merge: github.com/redwood/response-adapter/pull/412 — will merge after quick review and rollout to prod. Also adding an integration test to ensure envelope flag defaults to off for Hosted customers.
Ben - Infra: follow-up action: add a guard in deployment job to prevent unintended config keys from merging into Hosted profiles.
Olivia - CS: great. I'll send customer an apology + ETA for backfill and the postmortem once done.
Olivia - CS: todo list: 1) Confirm backfill window w/ infra 2) Share postmortem and credit recommendation 3) Confirm test coverage for envelope regressions.
Ben - Infra: assigning myself and Meera. Will update this thread when backfill completes. :thumbsup:
